statement: Share of firms using AI to produce goods or services >= 2x its 2025 average (Bloc A Census Bureau BTOS, 2027Q4)
status_at_phase_end: Series break: from the 2025-11-17 collection BTOS replaced 'in producing goods or services' with 'in any of its business functions' and started a new time series (level shift ~9-10% -> ~17%). The original-wording series the indicator names is discontinued; resolution needs a method decision (splice ratio or re-baseline). On the new series AI use rose from 17.3% (Nov 2025) to 24.2% (period ending 2026-11-01), +40% in ~11 months.

items.summary: Statistics office changed the core AI-use question wording (from 'in producing goods or services' to 'in any business function') and started a new time series; the original series ends in Nov 2025. The indicator's named series no longer exists for 2026-2027.
items.detail: Bloc A Census Bureau, 'BTOS AI Core Question Updates' (new series from data released 2025-12-04; old data kept in 'AI Core Questions (Original)' table). Published before the phase but governs every 2026 reading; included as context.

items.summary: First new-wording readings of 2026: ~17.7% of firms used AI in the two weeks ending 2026-01-11 (vs 17.3% at end-Nov 2025); expected use in six months ~22%.
items.detail: Bloc A Census BTOS biweekly release; values via programs.com tracker of Census data. Release date approximate (BTOS publishes biweekly, a few days after period end).

items.summary: Statistics-office research poster: as of April 2026 AI adoption ~18% (new wording), expected ~22% by autumn; adoption concentrated in information, professional services and finance; 66% of adopters use AI only to augment tasks.
items.detail: Bloc A Census BTOS AI supplement poster (National Academies, dated 2026-04-27). Supplement fielded 2025-11-17 to 2026-02-08, ~117,000 responding businesses.

items.summary: Statistics office released the full AI supplement and a story: Dec 2025-May 2026 AI use hovered between 17% and 20% (19.8% for period ending 2026-05-03); 37% of firms with 250+ employees use AI; little change among firms with <20 employees.
items.detail: Bloc A Census Bureau press release 'BTOS Data Release - May 7, 2026' and story 'Large Firms With at Least 20 Employees Biggest AI Users' (May 2026).

items.summary: Regional central-bank analysis: on the original wording, firm AI use in production was ~10% in late 2025, double mid-2024; under the broader wording it jumped to ~20% in early 2026. Implied 2025 average on the original series is roughly 8-9%.
items.detail: Federal Reserve Bank of Minneapolis, 'AI adoption in business grows steadily but unevenly' (2026; exact day not verified).

items.summary: Statistics office proposed repeating the AI supplement and moving generative-AI-use and AI-employment-impact questions into the core biweekly survey, plus a new question on AI's effect on new hires.
items.detail: Federal Register 2026-18304, BTOS information-collection request to OMB (comments by 2026-10-09).

items.summary: Latest reading before phase end: 24.2% of firms used AI in the two weeks ending 2026-11-01 (peak 24.6% two weeks earlier), up 6.9 pts from 17.3% in Nov 2025; expected use 27.6%. Largest gains among firms with 50-249 employees.
items.detail: Bloc A Census BTOS via programs.com tracker (updated 2026-11-06). Information 45.0%, Professional services 41.6%, Manufacturing 21.4%, Retail 19.1%.

items.summary: No comparable biweekly firm-AI-use series exists for Bloc B; only Bloc A data are available for this indicator.
items.detail: No NBS (Bloc B) high-frequency firm AI adoption series found.
